Subject: Finlytics POC - success criteria & next steps

Hi Samir / Lena —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps so we have a shared plan for the POC at a high level. I pasted the key items below — please flag anything I missed.

POC goals (what success looks like)
- Validate Redwood reduces per-token inference cost by >= 25% vs current setup while maintaining comparable generation quality for support-response templates.
- Achieve 95th-pctl latency <= 400ms for 512-token seqs under a synthetic 10 qps load.
- Confirm KV/prefix caching reduces repeated-context token consumption for top-10 flows.

Evaluation plan
- Week 0 (this week): access + data sample ingestion. Redwood SE to provision test endpoint and verify schema.
- Week 1: ingest 1M token sample, run baseline evaluation (latency & cost).
- Week 2: tune batching/quantization profile + run A/B vs baseline.
- Week 3: produce final runbook and recommendations.

Owners / ask list
- Finlytics: provide sample dataset (anonymized), endpoint allowlist IP (or VPN access), and a primary technical contact for infra (Lena?).
- Redwood: SE + infra setup (Marcus), baseline script & eval harness (Nikhil), weekly status updates (me).

Timeline / checkpoints
- Kickoff / access provisioning by 2026-03-03.
- Baseline run complete by 2026-03-10.
- Mid-POC check-in 2026-03-12.

Attachments: Redwood-POC-Plan.pdf (POC template & evaluation checklist), Finlytics-Data-Sample.csv (example schema).

Next steps: can you confirm the technical contact and whether you can share the sample dataset by end of day Tuesday (2026-03-03)? If yes, Marcus will start provisioning the test endpoints.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this running.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. This matches our internal view. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Success criteria: the cost target looks good; can we add qualitative metric "no more than 5% reduction in response helpfulness" measured via a 200-sample blind evaluation? I can coordinate our PM team to run that.
- Latency: 400ms p95 is acceptable for our SLA window (we target p95 < 500ms in prod). If you can hit 400ms that's great.
- Data share: we can provide an anonymized 500k-token sample by EOD Tue (2026-03-03). I'll attach a redacted sample.

Technical contact: Lena Morales (lena.morales@finlytics.com) is the infra lead and will provide allowlist details and a jumpbox if needed. Procurement loop: procurement@finlytics.com for any MSA/contract notes.

One ask: can Redwood provide a short script to run a baseline locally (we prefer to sanity-check before sharing large exports)? Marcus / Nikhil — can you share that?

Samir
